title: Creating and Rendering Forms
description: Define a form class and render it in a template.

slides.title: Defining a Simple Form
slides.content:
Create a `forms.py` file in your app (or define forms in `views.py`).

```python
from django import forms

class ContactForm(forms.Form):
    name = forms.CharField(max_length=100)
    email = forms.EmailField()
    message = forms.CharField(widget=forms.Textarea)
```

Each field corresponds to an HTML input. You can customize widgets (like `Textarea`) to change the rendering.

slides.title: Rendering Forms in Templates 🎨
slides.content:
In your view, instantiate the form and pass it to the template.

```python
from .forms import ContactForm

def contact(request):
    form = ContactForm()
    return render(request, 'contact.html', {'form': form})
```

In the template, you can render the whole form, individual fields, or manually loop.

```html
<form method="post">
    {% csrf_token %}
    {{ form.as_p }}
    <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

`as_p`, `as_table`, `as_ul` are shortcuts to wrap fields in paragraphs, table rows, or list items.

slides.title: Manual Rendering
Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Always include `{% csrf_token %}` in POST forms

Without it, Django will reject the submission with a 403 Forbidden error.
